correctness.rationale: A complete 90-word domain and exact 15-position-choice deletion shadows define the correct confusability graph. Explicit increasing-index clique search visits each clique uniquely; complete size histogram 1,90,1164,1788,144,0 proves optimum 4 and exact 144 equality count. A separate position-generated LCS dynamic program reproduces every clique count and rules out all 5-extensions. The witness 012201,102102,200211,211200 has disjoint deletion shadows. Exhaustive S3 x C2 group action yields 4 orbits of size 6 and 10 of size 12. Rational primal/dual variables with independently checked inequalities both sum to 5, establishing the LP optimum without floating point; fractional bound alone is not the integral upper proof.

value.rationale: The exact optimal two-deletion capacity and full 144-case/14-orbit equality structure give a natural short-block benchmark for uniformly repeated ternary symbols and four-symbol subsequence reads. A verified 5/4 integrality gap identifies why the obvious fractional shadow bound does not prove the sharp integer packing result, and the equality classification provides reproducible construction data. This is not a known-table recomputation or arbitrary slice: it resolves a natural smallest balanced ternary multipermutation two-deletion instance, with a nontrivial polyhedral obstruction.
